title: Phone readout uses the best installed voice instead of the default robotic one

requirements.text: On TTS init the app sets tts.voice to the highest-quality installed voice for the phone's language, preferring offline voices
requirements.check: manual: read the voice-pick code in MainActivity.kt

requirements.text: The picked voice's name and quality appear in logcat on app start
requirements.check: manual: adb logcat -s Genlock shows the picked voice name

requirements.text: When no ranked voice exists the app falls back to tts.language = Locale.getDefault()
TJ hears a smoother voice reading a reply on the Pixel
requirements.check: eye: TJ listens to a reply readout on the Pixel

requirements.text: The app builds and the JVM tests pass

evidence: MainActivity.kt pickVoice(): filters tts.voices by language, drops notInstalled, sorts quality desc, same country, offline, latency; setVoice(best)
pickVoice sets t.language = Locale.getDefault() first; setVoice only if a ranked voice exists
adb logcat -s Genlock on Pixel 10 Pro after restart: 'voice: en-us-x-tpf-local quality=400 network=false'

text: Installed on Pixel 10 Pro; picks en-us-x-tpf-local (QUALITY_HIGH, offline). Waiting on TJ to listen. TJ asked about our own voice instead of the phone's: options are on-device Kokoro/Piper via sherpa-onnx, or cloud neural TTS; both lose or change onRangeStart word timing that Walker uses for captions.

evidence: TJ is moving off the built-in voice entirely; the best-built-in pick stays only as the fallback until the Genlock voice reaches the phone

answers.observed: logcat on Pixel 10 Pro: voice: en-us-x-tpf-local quality=400 network=false
answers.cause: default voice for a locale was a lower-quality one; setVoice of the top-ranked fixes the pick
answers.absence: TJ never listened: waived, he is moving to the Genlock voice
answers.assumption: offline voices preferred over network ones
answers.falsify: a phone whose voices list is empty: falls back to language default
